Cold Open @VERSION@
==========================

Cold Open is a free, open-source screenwriting app. It reads and writes
Fountain and .fdx files, and it journals every keystroke, so a crash costs
you nothing. Your scripts are plain files: nothing you write here is
locked in.

This is an alpha, for testers. It is not signed by Apple or Microsoft yet,
so your system warns you the first time you start it (see below).

Source code: https://github.com/TheYungStump/cold-open
Licenses: the "licenses" folder (Cold Open is GPL-3.0-or-later).


Starting it
-----------

Windows: run the installer, or unzip the zip anywhere and double-click
"Cold Open.exe". SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC", because
the build isn't signed: click "More info", then "Run anyway". The
installer needs no administrator rights.

macOS: open the .dmg and drag Cold Open to Applications. The first time,
macOS refuses it, because it isn't notarized. Open System Settings >
Privacy & Security, scroll to the message about Cold Open, and click
"Open Anyway". (On macOS 12 to 14 you can also Control-click the app and
choose Open.) If macOS says the app is damaged, run this in Terminal, then
try again:
    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Cold Open.app"

Linux: install the .deb (sudo apt install ./cold-open_*.deb), or make the
AppImage executable and run it, or install the Flatpak:
    flatpak install --user ColdOpen-*.flatpak
The Flatpak can open scripts in your home folder. For another drive, run
    flatpak override --user --filesystem=/path/to/drive io.github.theyungstump.coldopen


The command-line tool
---------------------

coldopen converts, exports, compares and repairs scripts, and runs an MCP
server for AI agents (coldopen mcp). Type coldopen --help for the list.

- Windows installer: it's on your PATH; open a new terminal.
- Windows zip: it's next to Cold Open.exe.
- macOS: choose "Install the command-line tool" in the app's palette
  (Ctrl+K or Cmd+K), or link it yourself:
    ln -s "/Applications/Cold Open.app/Contents/MacOS/coldopen" ~/.local/bin/coldopen
- .deb: /usr/bin/coldopen.
- AppImage: run it as  ./ColdOpen-*.AppImage cli --help , or make a link
  named coldopen to the AppImage.
- Flatpak: flatpak run --command=coldopen io.github.theyungstump.coldopen


Measuring performance
---------------------

"Measure performance" in the palette (or  coldopen bench  in a terminal)
runs for about two minutes and writes two small files to your Downloads
folder. They hold your computer's model names and the times, and nothing
else. Please send them to us.


What to try
-----------

1. Write a scene. A new script starts on a scene heading. Enter and Tab
   move between elements; the bar at the top says what Enter and Tab will
   give next. Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on macOS) opens the palette, which lists every
   command and its shortcut.
2. Save with Ctrl+S (Cmd+S). The first save asks where.
3. Try to lose work. While typing, end the app hard: Task Manager >
   End task on Windows, Force Quit on macOS, or kill -9 on Linux. Start it
   again. If the script was saved, open it: a dialog says what was
   recovered. If it was never saved, the app offers it at start-up.
   Nothing that was on screen should be missing.
4. Let an AI agent edit the open script. With Claude Code:
       claude mcp add coldopen -- coldopen mcp
   Then ask it to open the script you have open in the app and make a
   change. You see the edit appear, a violet bar marks the changed block,
   and Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z) undoes it.
5. Export a PDF: Ctrl+Shift+E (Cmd+Shift+E).
6. Open an .fdx file, edit it, save it and open it again: it stays an
   .fdx file, and nothing in it should be lost.
7. Recovered versions (palette, or the start screen): changes Cold Open
   set aside instead of deleting. Restore opens one as a new script.


Settings and files
------------------

settings.json, keymap.json (your own shortcuts) and flow.json (your own
element flow) live in:
- Windows: %APPDATA%\Cold Open
- macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Cold Open
- Linux: ~/.config/coldopen

Scripts you haven't saved yet live in an "Unsaved" folder
(%LOCALAPPDATA%\Cold Open\Unsaved on Windows, ~/.local/share/coldopen on
Linux), with a crash journal. Uninstalling leaves these alone.

A script in a folder Cold Open can't write to opens as a copy in
"Unsaved"; use Save as to keep it somewhere else.


Reporting a problem
-------------------

Say which system you used, what you did, and what you expected. "Copy
version info" in About (palette) copies the version for you. If work went
missing, look in Recovered versions first. Keep the "Unsaved" folder and
any ".coldopen-journal" files next to your script (hidden on Windows):
they hold what was typed.
